description: Vulnerability classification decision criteria — rules for determining the correct classification label. Sourced from review_taxonomy.yaml (CLASS) and system_responsibility.md.

entries.title: Confirmed Vulnerability requires demonstrated exploitation + manual verification
entries.description: To classify as Confirmed Vulnerability, three conditions must ALL be met: (1) exploitation is demonstrated in the evidence, (2) evidence supports the vulnerability claim, and (3) manual verification was performed. If any condition is missing, the classification must be Potential Issue.
entries.action: Classification can be confirmed_vulnerability. For High/Critical severity, escalate to human for final confirmation (SLM proposes, human confirms).

entries.title: Potential Issue when vulnerability likely but not fully demonstrated
entries.description: When the vulnerability appears likely based on the finding description, but exploitation is not fully demonstrated or evidence is insufficient to confirm, the classification must be Potential Issue. This is the safe default for uncertain findings.
entries.action: Classification MUST be potential_issue. Do NOT upgrade to confirmed_vulnerability without sufficient evidence. Recommend human escalation for further testing.

entries.title: Informational when no direct vulnerability
entries.description: When the finding describes information disclosure, a best-practice observation, or a configuration recommendation without a direct exploitable vulnerability, the classification should be Informational.
conditions: information disclosure or best-practice observation only
entries.action: Classification is informational. Severity should be low or informational. No exploitation expected.

entries.title: False Positive requires evidence contradicting the claim
entries.description: To classify as False Positive, there must be evidence that the reported vulnerability cannot be reproduced, or evidence that directly contradicts the vulnerability claim. This is a human-only decision in v1.
entries.action: Flag for false_positive_detection. This is a HUMAN-ONLY decision in v1 — SLM must not classify as false_positive autonomously. Escalate to human reviewer.

entries.title: Never upgrade classification without sufficient evidence
entries.description: The SLM must never upgrade a classification from Potential Issue to Confirmed Vulnerability without sufficient evidence. This is a core safety principle. If evidence is borderline, keep as Potential Issue and escalate.
entries.action: Do NOT upgrade to confirmed_vulnerability. Keep as potential_issue. Escalate to human reviewer for final decision.

entries.title: Undetermined when classification is not possible
entries.description: When the finding cannot be classified into any of the four categories due to missing or contradictory information, use 'undetermined'. This preserves the safety principle of not guessing.
entries.action: Classification is undetermined. Escalate to human reviewer. Provide all available evidence for human judgment.
